title: Bidirectional A* Finds Fast Routes in Zürich!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* trace two search fronts across a street-map grid, meeting in the middle for a speed boost. The visualization highlights how heuristics and graph search cooperate to cut exploration dramatically.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ **Bidirectional A*** just got smarter in **Zürich (Kreis 11/11 Albisrieden)**!

On real street-map graphs, pathfinding becomes a **graph search** problem: intersections are nodes, streets are edges, and costs flow along weighted connections. With **Bidirectional A***, we run two A* searches simultaneously—one forward from the start and one backward from the goal—then **stop when the frontiers connect**, often reducing the explored area vs. classic single-direction A*. 🔍⚡

🧠 **Technical gist (what you’re seeing):**
• Each direction uses an **admissible heuristic** (e.g., straight-line distance on coordinates) to estimate remaining cost 🎯
• The algorithm balances **actual cost (g)** with **heuristic estimate (h)** using **f = g + h**
• When the two paths meet, we reconstruct the shortest route on the **same underlying weighted graph** 🗺️
